correctness.rationale: Deduplicate the special lines arising from edges. Graph connectedness makes their line-intersection incidence graph connected, so they can be ordered with each new line meeting the previous union at a configuration point. The first special line consumes at least three vertices and contributes affine dimension one. Any later line that increases affine dimension by one has exactly one previously used configuration point and therefore contributes at least two new vertices; a line with two old points lies in the old affine span. Hence \(n\ge3+2(d-1)\), giving \(d\le\lfloor(n-1)/2\rfloor\). For every tree, the diameter-end reduction removes two vertices while preserving a tree, either as a pendant two-edge path or as two sibling leaves; restoring them on a fresh line through the surviving anchor adds exactly one affine dimension and preserves all special-edge conditions. Induction from orders three and four attains the upper bound. The bundled finite tree enumeration checks the reduction logic only; it is not used as the infinite proof.
